chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: The weekend in Providence before the crash
summary: Cobb and his wife drive their new DeSoto with baby Lisette to Providence's Celebrity Club, scouting entertainers, and stay an extra day.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: All righty -- let me first tell you how I got there. My wife and I were sitting up back on Friday night. She called me Hoss -- that's another one of my nicknames.

Hoss, H-o-s-s. I told you I had many. She said, 'Hoss, let's go to Providence.' I said, 'Good,' because I heard there was something up there in the Celebrity Club, and we had friends up there, Donald and Madeline Griffith, and we called them up and, see, just like that, I made up my mind, and 6:30 the next morning we was up having coffee, getting ready to take off. I just bought this new car, first '56 Desoto push button. Remember the push button? And I called it -- I bought it for my Dungaree Doll, my daughter. She was -- when we had the accident, she was three months and 12 days old.
And we went on up to Providence and I went into the

Celebrity Club on a Saturday night, and I was getting ready to regroup my band FOR a little more entertainment, not just and I just musicianship -- (inaudible) everybody's great but nobody's entertaining. I'm getting ready to get what I want to get to have a little more life in the group. I spotted what I wanted to spotted and I told the guys, said, "I'll call you on Tuesday and let you know when to come down, and I'll have a rehearsal." (inaudible).

So I said to Griff -- who we were staying with. This is Madeline and Donald. "I'm leaving Sunday." He said, "Why don't you stay until Monday? You ain't got nothing to do." Well, I said, "I promised Ben Barth I was going to stop back through New Rochelle and see him on Sunday. That's my agent." He said, "Do you have to?" Well, I said, "I can call him and let him know I'll be in Monday, and I'll call him at the office on Monday." And he said, "Why don't you do that, just stay over? We hate to see you all leave."

So I did. I called Ben. I told him, said, "I'm not coming in today. I'll call you at the office," I said, (inaudible) whatever you've got at the office, (inaudible), and I told him what progress I'd made and what I found and what I intended to do. He said, "good."
